courseTitle: Applied AI Engineering (LLMs, RAG & Agentic AI)

topics.description: Understand what a large language model is and why it is the foundation of every other topic in this course. Start here before touching frameworks.
subtopics: Where we get LLMs from: hosted APIs vs private LLMs

topics.description: Learn how to choose a model for a task by comparing quality, speed and price instead of following hype.
subtopics: Benchmarks and what they actually measure
Costing per input and output token
Choosing the best provider for a task

topics.description: An LLM alone is limited. ChatGPT and Claude feel powerful because of the tools around the model, not because of the raw model.
subtopics: No tools by default: why raw LLMs cannot browse, calculate or act
How products add tools around the model
Privacy and data concerns with hosted models

theory: What is an LLM and how does it generate text?
Difference between a hosted LLM API and a private/self-hosted LLM.
What do LLM benchmarks measure and what are their limitations?
What is a knowledge cutoff and how do you work around it?
Why do raw LLMs hallucinate, and how can an application reduce it?
practical: Create free accounts on two LLM providers and get API keys.
Send the same prompt to two different models and compare the answers.

Track token usage and estimated cost for 20 API calls.
Build a model-selection cheat sheet for your own future projects.

topics.description: Tokens decide both cost and limits. The last two token types below are the most important for building efficient AI systems.
subtopics: Counting tokens before sending a request

topics.description: Control how creative or deterministic the model is and how long it can answer.
subtopics: Context window and what happens when it overflows

topics.description: Learn the different roles in a request and the different ways to call a model, including the cheaper batch route.
subtopics: Batch API for cost-effective bulk work

topics.description: Production systems must respect provider limits or they will fail under load.

theory: Explain input, output, cached input and cached write tokens.
What is the context window and what happens when a conversation exceeds it?
Explain temperature, top-p and top-k with examples.
Difference between a system prompt and a user prompt.

Call an LLM with temperature 0 and 1.5 and compare outputs.

Build a small token and cost tracker for every API call.
Create a reusable function that wraps the LLM API with logging.
Compare the same request across two providers using their native SDKs.
Build a command-line chatbot with configurable parameters.

topics.description: Write prompts that give reliable results. System and user prompts are the most important input you control.
You will use this daily. It makes LLM output machine-readable so code can depend on it.
Function calling lets the model request actions. Frameworks like LangChain and LangGraph are built on top of this, so if you skip it you will get lost later.
subtopics: Model decides which function to call
Executing the function in your backend
Sending the result back to the model

theory: Why is structured output important in production AI systems?
Explain few-shot prompting with an example.
How does function calling work end to end?
Why must the backend, not the model, execute the function?
How do frameworks like LangChain and LangGraph depend on function calling and structured output?
practical: Write a prompt template with variables for a summarization task.
Use few-shot examples to improve a classification prompt.
Force an LLM to return valid JSON for a given schema.
Define a Pydantic model and use it as the output schema.

Let the model choose between calling a tool and answering directly.
Build a resume parser that outputs structured JSON.
Build a meeting-notes extractor returning action items as a list.
Build a mini assistant combining structured output and function calling.

topics.description: Revise the Python you need to write clean production code, not just scripts.
Very important. AI apps wait on network calls all the time, and async lets one server handle many requests.
subtopics: Sync vs async: when to use which

topics.description: FastAPI is the preferred backend for AI apps. You do not need to memorize syntax, but you must grasp the concepts.
LLM tasks are slow, so long jobs must run outside the request cycle.
Every real AI product needs users, tokens and safe handling of secrets.
Speed and reliability layer for AI backends.
